Q: Dynamically change log levels across all instances A:

You can combine log4j2's ability to monitor its configuration for changes and automatically reload it and Kubernetes ConfigMaps to store the configuration and mount it as a file in your application. Updating the ConfigMap will apply the change to all application instances (i.e. pods) after the configured reload interval.

For instances, given the following ConfigMap which holds the log4j2 configuration (the example uses YAML, but XML works the same):

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: log4j2-config
data:
  log4j2.yml: |
    Configuration:
      monitorInterval: '10' # check config file for changes every 10 seconds
      Appenders:
        Console:
          name: Console
          # …
      Loggers:
        Root:
          level: info
          AppenderRef:
            - ref: Console
        Logger:
          - name: com.example
            level: warn
          - name: com.example.app
            level: debug

Once you have the ConfigMap, mount it in your application pods:

apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: your-app
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: your-app-image:latest
      volumeMounts:
      - name: logging-config
        mountPath: /config
        readOnly: true
  volumes:
  - name: logging-config
    configMap:
      name: log4j-config

Every time you update the ConfigMap, Kubernetes will eventually update the mounted files, making log4j2 reload the configuration after the configured interval (up to 10 seconds in my example, after Kubernetes has updated the mounted volume). It's not instantaneous and atomic across all pods, but should be good enough for most use cases. And it works without restarting or redeploying your application: you only need to roll out a new version of the ConfigMap and all pods will eventually see the updated configuration.

Unfortunately, there's no free lunch and this solution comes with some minor caveats:

  • Updates in the ConfigMap will overwrite any log level configuration via Spring's logging.level.* properties
  • Does not integrate well with the actuator/logging endpoint

If you choose this solution, I'd recommend to configure loggers exclusively via the log4j2 config file.

References:

  • https://logging.apache.org/log4j/2.x/soa.html#separate-config
  • Is it possible to reload log4j.xml / log4j.properties file dynamically in Tomcat?

Q: I have a picture with a mapped area that by clicking on it opens a mp4 video in a highslide frame A:

If you check file highslide-with-html.js then you see Version: 4.1.13 (2011-10-06)
so it is 15 years old (and probably there is no newer version) and maybe it can't work witn videos.

Maybe you should try example for YouTube Video which uses iframe to display videos.

<area   
# ... other parameters ....
onclick="return hs.htmlExpand(this, {objectType: 'iframe', width: 480, height: 385, allowSizeReduction: false, wrapperClassName: 'draggable-header no-footer', preserveContent: false, objectLoadTime: 'after'})"
/>

or at least

<area   
# ... other parameters ....
onclick="return hs.htmlExpand(this, {objectType: 'iframe'})"
/>

And this works for me in Firefox on Linux.

Q: How to completely clear the cache in Laravel A:

php artisan config:cache doesn't clear cache, but creates config cache. If you'll run first 4 commands from your list, all app cache will be cleared.

You may also want to clear cache, created by packages or composer or web server, it depends on what are you trying to achieve.

If you want to clear nginx cache, you can do this by deleting nginx cache directory, for example /var/nginx/cache/.

Q: `std::shared_ptr` vs `std::optional` for thread safe queue A:

Is it ok to implement this using the newer std::optional<T>?

Yes. You may implement this particular ThreadSafeQueue using std::optional.

This is also not a very efficient thread-safe queue. The book will tell you this as well.

Later in this book, you will learn that std::shared_ptr has some thread-safe properties built in, while std::optional has none. Once this thread safety is leveraged in your code, you will no longer be able to safely use std::optional.

Q: java.net.SocketException: Malformed reply from SOCKS server A:

To fix this:

1) Open Tools -> Internet Options in Internet Explorer (or alternatively, Control Panel Network Settings in Windows 7)

2) Open Connections tab

3) Click on LAN settings

4) If "Use a proxy server" is enabled, click Advanced and disable "Use the same proxy server for all protocols"

Q: How do I set the background to a solid color? When I use setContentView the screen is blank A:

Take a look at using a state list drawable as a background. Each item can point to a shape drawable that specifies a different background color. Alternatively, use a shape drawable as a background that points to a color state list as the solid color.

If the built-in attributes available for defining a state list drawable or a color state list are not right for your application, you can use the technique shown in this thread to define your own.
